heading.en: What can your pocket money buy?

hook.en: With ₹100, pens at ₹5 and notebooks at ₹10, which combinations can you buy? Your income and prices draw a line for you.
hook.kn: ₹100ರಲ್ಲಿ, ₹5ರ ಪೆನ್ನು ಮತ್ತು ₹10ರ ನೋಟ್‌ಪುಸ್ತಕ – ಯಾವ ಸಂಯೋಜನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಕೊಳ್ಳಬಹುದು? ಆದಾಯ ಮತ್ತು ಬೆಲೆಗಳು ನಿಮಗಾಗಿ ಒಂದು ರೇಖೆ ಎಳೆಯುತ್ತವೆ.

title.en: Define budget set and budget line
Find intercepts and slope of the budget line
Show changes in the budget set when income or prices change

say.en: With 100, rupees pens at 5 rupees and notebooks at 10, rupees which combinations can you buy? Your income and prices draw a line for you. In this lesson: Define budget set and budget line.
Find intercepts and slope of the budget line.
Show changes in the budget set when income or prices change.

body.en: A consumer with income M facing prices $p_1$ and $p_2$ can afford every bundle with $p_1x_1 + p_2x_2 \le M$. This collection is the *budget set*. Bundles that cost exactly M lie on the budget line $p_1x_1 + p_2x_2 = M$. It meets the axes at $M/p_1$ and $M/p_2$, and its slope is $-p_1/p_2$: the rate at which the market lets the consumer exchange good 2 for good 1.

narration.en: The budget set has all bundles the consumer can afford. The budget line has the bundles that cost exactly the income, and its slope is minus the price ratio.
narration.kn: ಅನುಭೋಗಿ ಕೊಳ್ಳಬಹುದಾದ ಎಲ್ಲ ಸಂಯೋಜನೆಗಳು ಆಯವ್ಯಯ ಗಣ. ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ಆದಾಯ ವೆಚ್ಚವಾಗುವ ಸಂಯೋಜನೆಗಳು ಆಯವ್ಯಯ ರೇಖೆಯಲ್ಲಿವೆ; ಅದರ ಇಳಿಜಾರು ಬೆಲೆ ಅನುಪಾತದ ಋಣ ಮೌಲ್ಯ.

say.en: The budget set has all bundles the consumer can afford. The budget line has the bundles that cost exactly the income, and its slope is minus the price ratio. Budget set: p 1x 1 plus p 2x 2 is less than or equal to M.
say.kn: ಅನುಭೋಗಿ ಕೊಳ್ಳಬಹುದಾದ ಎಲ್ಲ ಸಂಯೋಜನೆಗಳು ಆಯವ್ಯಯ ಗಣ. ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ಆದಾಯ ವೆಚ್ಚವಾಗುವ ಸಂಯೋಜನೆಗಳು ಆಯವ್ಯಯ ರೇಖೆಯಲ್ಲಿವೆ; ಅದರ ಇಳಿಜಾರು ಬೆಲೆ ಅನುಪಾತದ ಋಣ ಮೌಲ್ಯ.

say.en: Intercepts: M over p 1 and M over p 2.
Slope equals -p 1 over p 2 price ratio.
Income is 40 rupees, good 1 costs 5 and good 2 costs 4. Find where the line meets each axis.
Join the two intercepts. Everything on or below the line is affordable: that is the budget set.
If income rises to 60, both intercepts grow and the line shifts out parallel. The slope stays the same.
If only the price of good 1 falls to 4, the line pivots outward on the x-axis; the good 2 intercept stays at 10.

caption.en: With income M and prices p₁ and p₂, every bundle with p₁x₁ + p₂x₂ ≤ M is affordable (shaded). The budget line has slope −p₁/p₂. Change income to shift it parallel; change one price to swing it about the other axis.
caption.kn: ಆದಾಯ M, ಬೆಲೆಗಳು p₁, p₂. p₁x₁ + p₂x₂ ≤ M ಆದ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಕಟ್ಟುಗಳು ಕೈಗೆಟಕುವವು (ಛಾಯೆ). ಬಜೆಟ್ ರೇಖೆಯ ಇಳಿಜಾರು −p₁/p₂. ಆದಾಯ ಬದಲಿಸಿದರೆ ಸಮಾಂತರ ಸರಿಯುವಿಕೆ; ಒಂದು ಬೆಲೆ ಬದಲಿಸಿದರೆ ತಿರುಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: The budget set With income M and prices p 1 and p 2, every bundle with p 1x 1 plus p 2x 2 is less than or equal to M is affordable shaded. The budget line has slope -p 1 over p 2. Change income to shift it parallel; change one price to swing it about the other axis.
say.kn: ಆದಾಯ M, ಬೆಲೆಗಳು p 1, p 2. p 1x 1 plus p 2x 2 is less than or equal to M ಆದ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಕಟ್ಟುಗಳು ಕೈಗೆಟಕುವವು (ಛಾಯೆ). ಬಜೆಟ್ ರೇಖೆಯ ಇಳಿಜಾರು -p 1 over p 2. ಆದಾಯ ಬದಲಿಸಿದರೆ ಸಮಾಂತರ ಸರಿಯುವಿಕೆ; ಒಂದು ಬೆಲೆ ಬದಲಿಸಿದರೆ ತಿರುಗುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: If income rises (prices unchanged), both intercepts increase and the *budget* line shifts outward parallel to itself; a fall in income shifts it inward. If the price of good 1 falls, $M/p_1$ rises while $M/p_2$ is unchanged: the line rotates outward around its vertical intercept and becomes flatter. A rise in $p_1$ rotates it inward.

points.en: Equal % change in M, p₁, p₂ → no change

narration.en: A change in income shifts the budget line parallel. A change in the price of one good rotates the line around the other axis.
narration.kn: ಆದಾಯ ಬದಲಾದರೆ ಆಯವ್ಯಯ ರೇಖೆ ಸಮಾಂತರವಾಗಿ ಸರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂದು ಸರಕಿನ ಬೆಲೆ ಬದಲಾದರೆ ರೇಖೆ ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಅಕ್ಷದ ಬಿಂದುವಿನ ಸುತ್ತ ತಿರುಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.kn: ಆದಾಯ ಬದಲಾದರೆ ಆಯವ್ಯಯ ರೇಖೆ ಸಮಾಂತರವಾಗಿ ಸರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂದು ಸರಕಿನ ಬೆಲೆ ಬದಲಾದರೆ ರೇಖೆ ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಅಕ್ಷದ ಬಿಂದುವಿನ ಸುತ್ತ ತಿರುಗುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: Income ₹100, p₁ = ₹5, p₂ = ₹10. Write the budget line, find its intercepts and slope, and check whether bundles (8, 6) and (10, 6) are affordable.

steps.en: (8, 6) costs 40 + 60 = ₹100: on the budget line, affordable.

answer.en: Intercepts 20 and 10, slope −0.5; (8, 6) is affordable (on the line), (10, 6) is not.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Income ₹100, p₁ = ₹5, p₂ = ₹10. Write the budget line, find its intercepts and slope, and check whether bundles (8, 6) and (10, 6) are affordable.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Income 100, rupees p 1 equals 5, rupees p 2 equals 10 rupees. Write the budget line, find its intercepts and slope, and check whether bundles (8, 6) and (10, 6) are affordable.
Budget line: 5x 1 plus 10x 2 equals 100.
Intercepts: x 1 equals 100 over 5 equals 20, x 2 equals 100 over 10 equals 10; slope equals minus 5 over 10 equals minus 0.5.
(8, 6) costs 40 plus 60 equals 100 rupees: on the budget line, affordable.
(10, 6) costs 50 plus 60 equals 110 rupees is greater than 100 rupees: outside the budget set.
So the answer is Intercepts 20 and 10, slope minus 0.5; (8, 6) is affordable on the line, (10, 6) is not.
